newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate edges down 50 bps to 9.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate edges down 50 bps to 9.3 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average lending rate fell 50 basis points to 9.3 percent on Wednesday due to weaker bank demand for kuna funds against relatively high supply, money market dealers said.
They put new borrowings at 10.5 of 12.5 million kuna total settlements, which shrank from Tuesday's 77.3 million.
Call money loans were made at an unchanged rate of 9.0 percent while lenders charged 12 percent for one-month funds.

On Wednesday, commercial banks placed some of their excess liquidity in a new issue of central bank 35-day bills. The volume shrank to 64 million kuna from 166 million a week ago, but the bank said they already had a lot tied up in bills.
This also followed Monday's payment, which drained a total 3.155 billion kuna from the system, or some 44 million kuna more as the banks' deposits rose since a fortnight earlier.

The central bank again stayed out of the foreign exchange market. It calculated the kuna midrates for Thursday weaker at 5.3628 to the dollar and a touch firmer at 3.5612 to the mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
